caseLayout.case.json: id, title, apis[], permissions[], optional timeoutMs (default 20000); id equals directory name
caseLayout.manifest.json: MV3 manifest; runner fills name/version and adds only http://127.0.0.1/* for collector transport
caseLayout.case.js: ES module exporting async run(h), executed in the extension-owned runner.html
caseLayout.otherFiles: Copied verbatim into a disposable extension installation; shared harness.js, entry.js, runner.html and config.js reserved

installation: Fresh private disposable profile per case. Install unpacked extension, wait for background registration, open extension runner.html. Never reuse personal or installed browser profiles. Default no-op worker supplied only if case has none.

fixtures.b: http://localhost:<same-port>; distinct origin with independent host permission
fixtures.frames: same-origin and cross-origin frame.html?kind=same|cross, about:blank and srcdoc; names same,cross,blank,srcdoc
fixtures.network: Localhost only. No fixture CORS grant by default. Runner rejects non-localhost routed traffic and disables background networking. Production CSP and sandbox remain enabled.

harness.record(label,value): Append ordered JSON observation immediately, snapshot value; undefined encoded {$undefined:true}
harness.call(label,invoke): Record call and result/error, timing class and runtime.lastError; expected API errors captured with exact message; use assert for required setup results
harness.callback(label,invoke): Record callback arguments, synchronous/asynchronous timing, lastError in callback and following microtask
harness.event(event,predicate,timeoutMs): Register immediately, resolve argument array on match, remove listener on completion/timeout; default 5000ms
harness.openTab(url): Create inactive tab and wait for completed load, returning tab; timeout 10000ms
harness.host(operation,args): POST capability-token collector /control; engine adapter must implement case-required operations or fail explicitly
harness.sleep(ms): Bounded case-local delay; no wall-clock measurements in observations
harness.assert(condition,message): Fail case on unmet setup or synchronization precondition

transport: config.js provides origins and collector URL containing per-run random capability. POST JSON /complete {status:complete|error,observations:[{label,value}],error?}. Collector bound to loopback, max 2 MiB, one terminal completion. Host RPC errors use non-2xx JSON {error}. Completion is sent by entry.js after run settles.
timeout: Runner enforces case timeout including installation. Timeout, thrown setup error, launch failure or collector failure produces status:error and nonzero exit. Partial/error transcripts never replace references. External runner process must additionally have a hard timeout.
output: One UTF-8 JSON file <case-id>.json: {schemaVersion:1,caseId,engine:{name,version,playwrightVersion?,chromiumRevision?},status,observations,error?}. Chromium version present in every Chromium transcript. Stable sorted object keys; observation arrays preserve order. normalize.mjs maps origins, extension IDs, typed runtime IDs and timestamps without hiding error text.
comparison: diff.mjs REFERENCE ACTUAL [ALLOWLIST] emits per-case pass/deviation/fail. Cross-engine metadata differs freely; Chromium check requires same engine metadata. deviations.json entries require caseId, engine, exact JSON-pointer path, expected, actual, reason and source. Unexpected or stale deviations fail; no wildcard ignores. Empty allowlist until actual second-engine evidence exists.

hostOperations.consoleMessages: Return observed console and CDP Log entries as {type,text}[]; cases select relevant diagnostics, deduplicating duplicate delivery.
hostOperations.stopBackground: Stop only the extension background in this disposable case profile through native engine lifecycle control; return {stopped:true}; case independently verifies port disconnect.
hostOperations.invoke-action: Activate case tabId and invoke its real extension action. Chromium uses browser CDP Extensions.triggerAction with actual tab target obtained by Target.getTargets filter; no synthetic onClicked event or grant injection. Return {supported:true,method}; case requires action event, grant and revocation.

nodeRunner.command: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/crynta/Dev/zephium-linux/audit/target node eval/webext-conformance/run-node.mjs --check [--case ID] [--output DIR] [--host EXECUTABLE]
nodeRunner.dependency: This checkout by default; optional --runtime-root PATH selects another checkout explicitly. Builds its locked tests/js_e2e.rs host and records that checkout revision; --host must be a matching already-built host.
nodeRunner.execution: Same case.js and shared harness in fresh Node vm realms using actual generated bindings and byte envelopes through Rust stdio_host. The fake browser models tab/window/action state and deterministic single-document loading, not native page execution or network. Manifest permissions, resource inventory and locale catalogs are passed into the runtime before contexts bind. Runtime-message and port cases load the original background.js in a distinct authenticated realm. Manual host epoch and realm Date.now both 1000000. Session storage access loads the original API-only content.js in an independently authenticated fake content principal after fake tab creation. This qualifies principal enforcement, not native content injection.
nodeRunner.limitations: node-plan.mjs classifies all 57 cases, with explicit reasons for unavailable cases; output/coverage/inventory.json preserves that inventory. Real page/network/worker/world injection is not simulated, native event acceptance is untested, and DNR metadata cases remain unavailable-runtime because no DNR backend is installed. --host matching is the caller responsibility.

partialCases.scripting-register-lifecycle: Registration metadata and refusals only. Five native injection calls (ten observations) are omitted explicitly; result is always labelled partial. Oracle observations are projected by validated labels without modifying reference files.

ci: check.sh is the bounded CI entry point. Automatic hosted job deferred: checked reference includes Linux ARM64 getPlatformInfo and allocator-sensitive session bytes; current hosted Ubuntu job is x86_64. Do not silently normalize genuine platform facts. Run on the matching host or qualify a separate reference before wiring CI.
normalization: Identity placeholders retain equality relationships. Tab/window IDs in exact known error templates are replaced without changing punctuation or other words; UUID document IDs and fixture HTTP/HTTPS origins are mapped. Rule IDs, alarm periods, byte counts, platform facts, and observation order remain evidence. Concurrent cross-frame event collection is projected into ordered per-frame sequences explicitly in case code.
